messages:
maya: Hey team — provisioning request + help debugging a weird pod density failure on the GKE GPU pool in asia-southeast1. We hit ENI/alias-ip exhaustion during a smoke test. Can someone raise the relevant quota increases and advise on a short-term mitigation?

raj: Which quotas exactly? GPU quota or IP ranges?

maya: Both. Observed two issues: (1) project GPU quota in asia-southeast1 is at 16 GPUs, we need 48 for the nodepool plan. (2) The nodepool uses alias IP secondary ranges and we ran out of usable pod IPs when scaling to 100 nodes because of fragmentation — GKE max-pods-per-node is 32 so we needed larger secondary range but cluster was created with /20 and multiple nodepools are eating it.

adrian: For GPUs: submit a support/quota increase in the cloud console for "NVIDIA A100 (or equivalent)" in asia-southeast1. For alias IPs, we can either expand the secondary range or create a new VPC subnet for the GPU nodepool. Expanding is easier but requires IP planning.

maya: Filed a request ticket draft, copying it here: 

```
Project: redwood-inference-prod
Quota: 'NVIDIA A100 (a2) GPUs'
Region: asia-southeast1
Current: 16
Requested: 80
Reason: onboarding Dedicated GPU nodepool for inference, steady steady-state throughput; will be used for latency-critical workloads with autoscaling policies.
```

raj: Add estimated monthly spend and contact PO so quota team prioritizes it. Also ask for increase to alias IP secondary range size and for VPC SKU allowances if needed.

maya: Good call. Estimated monthly GPU cost (on-commit discount) ~ $35k/mo. Adding that to the ticket and pinging finance.

infra-bot: deploy-check: new nodepool creation attempt failed: PodCIDR capacity exhausted (secondary range) — aborting.

sam: Short-term mitigation: create a temporary GPU nodepool in europe-west1 (lower quota limits we can bump faster) and route traffic there while quota is processed. Or lower max-pods-per-node on large nodes to increase allocation efficiency? Note: lowering max-pods increases per-node IP usage but might reduce fragmentation depending on range alignment.

adrian: Another option: use GKE VPC-native with custom-subnet and reserve a /19 for pod ranges, then create a dedicated secondary range for the GPU pool. That avoids touching existing nodepools. But requires downtime planning for routed services behind LB.

maya: @raj can you file the quota request with the updated numbers (80 GPUs, /19 alias IP expansion in project redwood-inference-prod, request more EIPs for ExternalLB)? I'll include cost/PO and urgency: P1 because Dedicated rollout depends on it.

raj: On it. I'll also request an increase to "Reserved static external IP" quota for the project (we need +10 for Canary LB). Linking GCP quota page: https://console.cloud.google.com/iam-admin/quotas?project=redwood-inference-prod

cost-ops: FYI — please tag the ticket with billing code INF-GPU-23 and include committed spend estimate, otherwise quota support asks for it.

maya: Thanks. Also can we add a temporary autoscaler policy to cap burst to avoid hitting pod density until quotas are resolved? Example command I ran that failed: 

```bash
# attempted nodepool create
gcloud container node-pools create gpu-pool --cluster=prod-cluster --region=asia-southeast1 \\n  --accelerator type=nvidia-tesla-a100,count=1 --num-nodes=10 --max-pods-per-node=32 \\n  --node-labels=workload=gpu --node-taints=gpu=true:NoSchedule \\n  --node-version=1.28.10-gke.1200 --enable-autoscaling --min-nodes=1 --max-nodes=100 \
  --machine-type=n2-standard-16 --disk-size=200 --node-ip-alias --cluster-secondary-range-name=pods-secondary-gpu
```

adrian: Good. After raj files the quota request, I can prep the /19 secondary range proposal with exact subnet math and a migration plan.

maya: Great. Thanks everyone. I'll update the thread with the quota ticket number once submitted. :thumbsup:
